title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LA1RD_1LA1LF_0RE---_1RA1RE_0RB0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LA1RD_1LA1LF_0RE---_1RA1RE_0RB0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. The head sweeps over the whole tape, which is made of runs of 01; a big repeated block at the left end grows and shrinks again and again. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the halting configurations and no halt in the first 107 steps. The structure below is observed in simulations, not proved. No halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 55,261 cells have been visited and 33,117 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.515).

claims.title: B never reads 1 with a 1 to its right (so far)
claims.text: The only halting entry is D reading a 1, and D is entered only from B>1 (write 1, move right): the machine halts exactly when B>1 1 occurs. In the first 108 steps D is entered 10,419,815 times, always onto a 0.

claims.title: Runs of 01 and a breathing end block
claims.text: The tape is runs (01)^k separated by single 0s, with k mostly 2, 3, 5, 8 or 11. At the left end a block (01010010101)^m (runs of 2 and 3 alternating) appears again and again: m grows (to 85 at step 1,448,288, to 339 at step 38,516,556) and is then eaten back down to 0, about nine words every sixty left-end visits (m = 78, 69, 61, 53, 44, 36, 27, 18, 9 at sixty-visit intervals from step 1,705,608), seen as rotations of the same word.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The end block's growth and decay look regular, but between two such cycles the tape is rewritten irregularly, and the run lengths that come out of each cycle have not been predicted. A proof would need either a rule for the whole cycle in terms of the run lengths or an invariant language for runs of 01 (which window-CTL with K ≤ 7 did not find).

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LC_1LA0RE_0LD---_1LB1LD_1RB1RF_0LA0RB up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine writes 0101… in runs separated by single 0s, and sweeps back and forth over them. At the left end a long repeated word builds up and is eaten away again, over and over; the rest of the tape is rewritten with no pattern found so far.

facts.text: No halt, checked by Lean's kernel (10<sup>7</sup> by compiled code).
No halt in the C simulator.
Entries into the halting state D in 10<sup>8</sup> steps, all onto a 0.

sections.heading: The one way to halt
html: The only halting entry is D reading a 1. D is entered only from B reading a 1 (B writes 1 and moves right), so the machine halts exactly when B>1 1 occurs. In the first 108 steps D is entered 10.4 million times, always onto a 0; the most common windows are 101[0]010, 101[0]011, 101[0]100, 111[0]100 and 111[0]101, about 2 million each.

sections.heading: Runs of 01, and a block that breathes
html: When the head reaches a new cell at the left end the tape reads, for instance,

Nearly everything is runs of 01 with a single 0 between them, here of length 5, 8, 8, 5, 8, …; the word 01010010101 is a run of 2 followed by a run of 3. Sixty left-end visits later the block reads (10101010100)^78 (the same word seen from another phase), then 69, 61, 53, 44, 36, 27, 18, 9, and at step 4,678,768 it is gone. Later it builds up again (116 at step 26,755,844, 339 at step 38,516,556) and is eaten again.
The rest of the tape is rewritten between cycles without a visible rule. Nothing here is proved.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.515).
After 109 steps the tape spans 55,261 cells (13,525 left of the start, 27,241 right), with a density of 1s of 0.599.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Bouncer over runs of 01 separated by single 0s (run lengths mostly 3, 5, 8, 11); at the left end an 11-cell word 01010010101 repeats up to a few hundred times, grows, and is then eaten back, again and again, while the rest of the tape changes irregularly. No regime proved.
family: bouncer over runs of 01 with a growing and shrinking end block
